title: Article 142 — Enforcement of decrees and orders of Supreme Court and orders as to discovery, etc.

content.overview: Article 142 provides that the Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it, and any decree so passed or order so made shall be enforceable throughout the territory of India in such manner as may be prescribed by or under any law made by Parliament and, until provision is so made, in such manner as the President may by order prescribe. Subject to law by Parliament, the SC shall have power to make any order for the purpose of securing the attendance of any person, the discovery or production of any documents, or the investigation or punishment of any contempt of itself.
content.glance: SC may pass any decree/order necessary for complete justice; enforceable throughout India. Ancillary powers as to attendance, discovery, contempt.
content.study:
Article 142(1) is the ‘complete justice’ power — a unique constitutional power enabling the SC to mould relief as necessary in causes before it. Enforcement is throughout India as prescribed by parliamentary law or, until then, Presidential order.

Article 142(2): powers as to attendance of persons, discovery/production of documents, and investigation/punishment of contempt of the Court, subject to parliamentary law.

Examination: complete justice; nationwide enforcement; attendance/discovery/contempt powers; subject to parliamentary law where indicated.

sections.heading: Key powers
sections.body:
1. Decree or order necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before the SC.
2. Enforceable throughout India (as prescribed by parliamentary law or Presidential order).
3. Orders for attendance, discovery/production of documents, and contempt of the Court (subject to parliamentary law).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the ‘complete justice’ power under Article 142?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 142, the Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it. Such decree or order is enforceable throughout the territory of India in the manner prescribed by or under parliamentary law or, until then, by Presidential order. The Court also has powers as to attendance of persons, discovery or production of documents, and contempt of itself, subject to law made by Parliament.

keyTakeaways: Art 142: complete justice power; enforcement throughout India.
